extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media scholars, Nieman Reports readers, and potential contributors/pitchers
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive/about page for the Nieman Reports publication summarizing its mission, history, editorial focus, and recognitions. Useful for understanding the publication's aims and reputation when deciding whether to read, cite, or pitch work to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial mission
rubrics_metrics.description: “To promote and elevate the standards of journalism.” (The page states the editorial mission mirrors that of the Nieman Foundation.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nieman Reports is a website and quarterly print publication whose mission is to promote and elevate journalistic standards. This mission is the primary evaluative lens implied for the publication's content and curation; material published or solicited should align with raising or examining journalistic standards. The page lists many awards and recognitions (Mirror Awards, Bart Richards Award, Sigma Delta Chi Awards, EPPY, Folio Eddie, SFJ Excellence-in-Features) as evidence of achieving high standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial focus: thought leadership and watchdog journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers thought leadership in journalism and hosts articles from the Nieman Watchdog Project, which published pieces about how journalists can hold those in power to account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content emphasis is on pieces that advance thinking about journalism practice, media criticism, ethics, and accountability reporting. The Watchdog Project (founded 1996) is highlighted as a home for watchdog reporting. Examples of topics recognized on the page include media criticism, commentary, feature journalism, and reporting on diversity and newsroom leadership (as evidenced by award-winning pieces listed).
